title: SRMIST Licenses Patented Polyherbal Anti-Diabetic Formulation to Dr. ShreeVarma’s Wellness
summary: SRMIST has licensed its patented polyherbal anti-diabetic formulation, developed at its IIISM, to Dr. ShreeVarma’s Wellness in a non-exclusive deal worth ₹125 lakhs.
body_html:
Chennai, 20 November 2026: SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) has signed a non-exclusive licensing agreement with Dr. ShreeVarma’s Wellness Pvt. Ltd for the manufacture and marketing across India of its patented polyherbal formulation for the management of diabetes. The agreement, which has a lifetime value of ₹125 lakhs, marks a step in taking traditional-medicine research from the laboratory to the marketplace.

The agreement was signed at Ramada Plaza by Wyndham, Guindy, with Dr. T. R. Paarivendhar, Chancellor, SRMIST, presiding over the ceremony. Prof. C. Muthamizhchelvan, Vice Chancellor, and Dr. S. Ponnusamy, Registrar, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, were present, along with Dr. ShreeVarma, Founder and Chairman, and Dr. Henoc Marceau, Director, of Dr. ShreeVarma’s Wellness Pvt. Ltd.

The formulation was developed by Dr. Sathish Kumar, Dean, Interdisciplinary Institute of Indian System of Medicine (IIISM), SRMIST, and his research team. It combines herbs that work together to help manage Diabetes Mellitus. Besides helping to lower blood sugar levels, it shows strong antioxidant activity and is designed to protect the kidneys and heart, helping to reduce the risk of diabetes-related complications.

The SRM Technology Transfer Office (SRM TTO) handled the licensing process from start to finish. It worked with the inventors, negotiated terms with the industry partner, and drafted and executed the agreement, and it will monitor licence milestones and compliance throughout the term. The office supports the transfer of inventions to industry through technology licensing, option agreements and industry-academia co-creation of technologies.

According to the institute, SRMIST has so far filed 1,171 patents, of which 1,107 have been published and 638 granted, a filing-to-grant conversion rate of over 75 per cent. The institute said it aims to become a source of transferable technologies through industry partnerships and live labs that let students and researchers follow the journey from idea to market.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. T. R. Paarivendhar said, “Research truly succeeds only when it leaves the laboratory and reaches the people it was meant to serve. This licence shows what can be achieved when our researchers and industry partners work towards the same goal.” He congratulated Dr. Sathish Kumar and his team and thanked the SRM Technology Transfer Office for guiding the agreement.

Dr. Sathish Kumar said, “Our aim was not only to develop a formulation, but to develop one that can be useful in people’s everyday lives. Diabetes affects the whole body over time, so we focused on a combination of herbs that work together, not just on bringing blood sugar down.”

Dr. ShreeVarma said, “We are honoured to partner with SRMIST and to be entrusted with a formulation that has come out of such careful research. Our responsibility now is to take it to the people who can benefit from it, and to do so with the same care and quality that went into developing it.”
